A reproducible parity protocol should freeze fixtures for all four categories: identical raw histories, truncated left-padded item-ID tensors, ordered candidate IDs, saved ID mappings, architecture configuration, and checkpoint SHA-256. Load the same category checkpoint into training-side and exported implementations with strict state-dict loading; compare parameters and buffers exactly. Include singleton, mixed-length, maximum-length, repeated-item, and explicitly handled empty histories. These are proposed application checks, grounded in PyTorch’s [reproducibility guidance](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.15/notes/randomness.html).

Packing requires special care: compact nonpadding events into chronological prefixes before `pack_padded_sequence`, pass CPU lengths and `enforce_sorted=False`, and preserve batch order. Packing left-padded tensors directly truncates valid suffix events. For left-aligned-to-the-right outputs, gather the maximum nonpadding index—never `count-1`; packed GRU `h_n[-1]` represents the final state of a unidirectional GRU. Compare packed execution against individually unpadded sequences, then compare exported execution against the training implementation. See [packing semantics](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.utils.rnn.pack_padded_sequence.html) and [GRU outputs](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.modules.rnn.GRU.html).

Run both implementations with `eval()` plus `inference_mode()`, matching device, dtype, batch shape, autocast and TF32 settings. Capture embeddings, GRU outputs/hidden states, readout and candidate logits using hooks; recursively snapshot tensors with `detach().clone()` because [detach shares storage](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.15/generated/torch.Tensor.detach.html). Compare scores in supplied candidate order, permutation consistency, top-10 IDs and tie handling. Record maximum absolute/relative errors and predefined tolerances; an FP32 starting point is `rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-6`, not a universal guarantee. Separately test deployment precision: [PyTorch documents numerical differences](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.15/notes/numerical_accuracy.html) across batching, devices and precision modes.
